# Summit Mergers

> Summit Mergers LLC is a boutique buy-side M&A brokerage. It introduces vetted private equity groups, family offices and strategic acquirers to owners of established, profitable service businesses ($2M–$50M in annual revenue) and supports a confidential sale through closing. The buyer pays Summit's fee at closing, so sellers pay nothing upfront or at closing. Summit recommends owners have their own attorney and CPA review final terms.

Industries served include HVAC, access control and security, fencing, professional services, technology, healthcare services and manufacturing. Most transactions close within 3 to 6 months of engagement.

Contact: info@summitmergers.com · (845) 402-6614

## Pages

- [Home](https://summitmergers.com/): services, the four-step sale process, fees and FAQs for business owners
- [Sell Your HVAC Business](https://summitmergers.com/sell-hvac-business.html): for HVAC company owners ($2M–$50M revenue) preparing to retire. How HVAC companies are valued (EBITDA/SDE multiples driven by maintenance agreements, owner dependence, technician retention, clean financials), the five steps of a sale, and confidential introductions to private equity, family office and strategic buyers. No fee to the seller.
- [Selling Your HVAC Company to Private Equity](https://summitmergers.com/sell-hvac-company-to-private-equity.html): why PE buys HVAC companies, platform vs add-on roll-ups, what PE looks for, deal structure (cash, rollover equity, earnouts, escrow), what changes after closing, PE vs family office vs strategic buyers, questions to ask
- [HVAC Business Valuation](https://summitmergers.com/hvac-business-valuation.html): adjusted earnings × multiple, SDE vs EBITDA, add-backs, value drivers, why published HVAC multiples disagree, how to raise value in 1–3 years. Summit does not sell valuations.
- [Do I Need a Business Broker?](https://summitmergers.com/do-i-need-a-business-broker.html): when a broker helps vs selling on your own, sell-side vs buy-side brokers and who pays, questions to ask, red flags
- [How to Prepare Your HVAC Business for Sale](https://summitmergers.com/prepare-hvac-business-for-sale.html): 12-point checklist for HVAC owners ($2M–$50M revenue) planning to sell in 1–3 years: clean financials and add-backs, written maintenance agreements, owner dependence, technician retention, licenses, fleet records, and what buyers request in diligence. Summit does not sell readiness reports; no fee to the seller.
- [How to Sell an HVAC Business Confidentially](https://summitmergers.com/sell-hvac-business-confidentially.html): for owners of $2M–$50M HVAC companies; who needs to know and when, NDAs before buyers learn your name, sharing numbers without names, what buyers eventually need to see, and what to do if employees or customers hear about the sale. Confidentiality cannot be guaranteed. No fee to the seller.
- [What Happens to Employees When You Sell an HVAC Company to Private Equity](https://summitmergers.com/sell-hvac-employees-after-private-equity-sale.html): for owners of $2M–$50M HVAC companies; what usually stays the same for technicians and staff, what can change after a private equity deal, and what to ask a buyer about pay, benefits and your own role before signing. No fee to the seller.
- [How to Sell a Plumbing Business](https://summitmergers.com/sell-plumbing-business.html): for owners of $2M–$50M plumbing companies; what drives value (service vs. new construction, license holder, commercial contracts, owner dependence), plumbing-specific issues buyers check, who buys, and how a confidential sale works. No fee to the seller.
- [How to Sell an Electrical Contracting Business](https://summitmergers.com/sell-electrical-contracting-business.html): for owners of $2M–$50M electrical contracting companies; what drives value (service vs. project mix, backlog quality, bonding, licensed foremen, customer concentration), electrical-specific issues buyers check (license, contract assignability, work in progress and retainage), who buys, and how a confidential sale works. No fee to the seller.
- [How to Sell a Security or Alarm Company](https://summitmergers.com/sell-security-company.html): for owners of $2M–$50M security, alarm and access control companies; why recurring monthly revenue (RMR), contract quality, attrition and monitoring arrangements drive value, security-specific issues buyers check (subscriber contract assignability, central station, licensing), who buys, and how a confidential sale works. No fee to the seller.
- [How to Sell a Fencing Company](https://summitmergers.com/sell-fencing-company.html): for owners of $2M–$50M fence installation and repair companies; what drives value (residential vs. commercial mix, product mix, job-level margins, crew stability, equipment and yard inventory, customer concentration), fencing-specific issues buyers check (backlog, materials cost pricing, licensing, insurance), who buys, and how a confidential sale works. No fee to the seller.
- [Sell Your Business and Retire](https://summitmergers.com/sell-and-retire.html): for owners of $2M–$50M service businesses who are ready to retire; what's included and how the confidential process works
- [Asset Sale vs. Stock Sale for an HVAC Company](https://summitmergers.com/asset-vs-stock-sale-hvac.html): guide to how each structure is taxed (depreciation recapture, C-corp double tax), why buyers prefer asset deals, and what to ask a CPA before signing an LOI
- [For Founders](https://summitmergers.com/founders.html): how Summit works with owners selling a service business
- [For Investors](https://summitmergers.com/investors.html): curated lower-middle-market deal flow for PE firms and family offices
- [About](https://summitmergers.com/about.html): who Summit Mergers LLC is, who pays the fee (the buyer), timeline, industries and contact details in plain text
- [Deals Closed](https://summitmergers.com/deals.html): completed transactions
